recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片右側一顆大型母細胞，核圓、染色質細緻，深藍色細胞質緊貼核周並帶細顆粒感；中間及周圍有多顆比紅血球小不了多少、淡藍無顆粒或帶粉紅顆粒的巨大異常血小板，配合 CML 病史符合巨核母細胞急變。
features: Large blast (right) with round nucleus, finely granular chromatin, and a thin rim of deeply basophilic cytoplasm
Small cytoplasmic bleb/attached platelet-like fragment at the blast margin
Multiple giant, pale blue, hypogranular platelets approaching red cell size (center and lower left)
Occasional platelet with clustered pink-purple granules and a small platelet clump (left)
Red cells with rouleaux-like stacking in thicker areas and scattered echinocytes
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a large blast with a round nucleus, finely granular chromatin, and a narrow rim of deeply basophilic cytoplasm with a small marginal cytoplasmic bleb. Several giant, pale blue, hypogranular platelets approaching the size of red cells are present, along with a few granular platelets. Red cells show scattered echinocytes and stacking in thicker areas. Blast lineage cannot be established morphologically, but in a patient with known CML and flow cytometry demonstrating CD41/CD61-positive blasts, findings are consistent with megakaryoblastic blast crisis with dysplastic giant platelets.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts may contain azurophilic granules or Auer rods and are MPO positive, whereas megakaryoblasts are MPO negative and express CD41/CD61.
Lymphoblasts lack cytoplasmic blebs and are accompanied by normal-sized platelets, and they express TdT with B- or T-lineage markers.
Congenital giant platelets occur without circulating blasts or leukocytosis.
Myelofibrosis shows teardrop cells, nucleated red cells, and giant platelets with only low blast counts and no BCR::ABL1 fusion.
